The text gives the population bases: 3,600 up to the end of 1882; 5,000 for 1882–1889; 5,274 for 1890. Column heads supplied from the printed line 'deaths registered … death-rate … per 1,000'.]
footnotes: (*) The census taken in 1880 gave 1,171 men, 502 women and 524 children; this, however, was limited to the Settlements North of the Yang-king-pang, and did not include the shipping. Before this the last census of the shipping was taken in 1870, and gave the number 1,101; the foreign population on the French Concession was estimated at the same time at 316. These figures give a total of 3,614.

(†) The census of 1885 for the Settlement North of the Yang-king-pang gave 1,775 men, 1,011 women, and 887 children; for the foreign shipping at this time 893 individuals were returned, chiefly adult males. If to these numbers 444 be added, the return made for the French Concession in 1890, the resulting total is 5,010.
